summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop during warm surge caused by sidecar memory leak and autoscaler gap
description:
Issue summary: LensAI reported sudden throughput drop and elevated p99 latencies for their dedicated pool (pool-id: lens-prod-1) during a warm surge window. Impact: several customer routes experienced queueing and fallback to lower-tier model variants; user-facing API timeouts observed at ~10:00 UTC.

Impact: Customer-facing latency increase (p95 -> p99 jump), increased request queue depth, and transient 5xx errors from internal queuing timeouts. This is a dedicated-pool customer (dedicated GPU capacity with pinned slots).

Environment: prod-us-east dedicated cluster servicing LensAI (us-east-1). Affected model variants: redwood-22B-quant (primary), psi-13B (fallback).

Initial hypothesis: warm surge + many short streams caused sidecar agent memory growth -> heartbeat drop -> autoscaler did not see correct utilization -> delayed reattachment of GPU slots -> noisy neighbor-like starvation.

Top-level ask: investigate root cause of autoscaler gap and sidecar OOMs, provide mitigation steps and an ETA for customer recovery.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have a dedicated pool with pinned slots and sidecar-agent enabled for prefetch/prefill behavior.
2) Replay a mixed workload with many short streaming requests (median length ~15 tokens) followed by periodic medium bursts (400-800 tokens) over 2-3 minutes to simulate warm surge.
3) Observe sidecar-agent memory growth in agent metrics; after ~8-12 minutes, heartbeat rate to scheduler degrades and allocation updates stop.
4) Autoscaler fails to expand pool due to missing heartbeat-derived metrics; p99 latency climbs and queued requests accumulate.
5) Restarting the sidecar or killing the leaking process restores heartbeat and allocations recover within 2-5 minutes.
Note: reproduced in a staging harness with smaller GPUs; requires high churn of short streams + periodic longer streams to surface the leak symptomatically.
observed_behavior: During the event sidecar-agent memory RSS for multiple nodes increased steadily until OOM killer reclaimed memory on 2 hosts. Heartbeat metrics from those hosts stopped reporting CPU/queue/utilization. Autoscaler interpreted lack of telemetry as idle (or unhealthy) and did not make new slot attachments; scheduler left several requests queued. p95 increased modestly but p99 jumped 4x and timeouts (504) seen on customer side. No driver crashes or GPU OOMs recorded; issue localized to sidecar process.
expected_behavior: Sidecar-agent should maintain steady memory usage, keep heartbeats alive, and autoscaler should be able to read utilization to scale pool as demand increases. During warm surges autoscaler should add slots within configured SLO and scheduler should not leave client requests queued beyond configured queuing_window.

Relevant excerpts:
- Mar 10 09:38:22 sidecar[lens-prod-1-node-3]: rss=420MB; streams=18; prefetch=on
- Mar 10 09:44:11 sidecar[lens-prod-1-node-3]: rss=880MB; streams=44; prefetch=on
- Mar 10 09:50:05 kernel: Out-Of-Memory: Kill process 4321 (sidecar) total-vm=...
- Mar 10 09:50:07 scheduler: heartbeat-missed node=lens-prod-1-node-3 duration=00:00:22

- Mar 10 09:52:10 scheduler: reattach-request node=lens-prod-1-node-3 status=ok
- Mar 10 09:54:30 cs: Customer reported degraded p99 and brief 504s

Logs indicate a memory growth pattern on the sidecar followed by OOM, missed heartbeats, and a short autoscaler gap that delayed slot reattachment.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:55 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Acknowledged issue with customer and opened ticket. Collected initial logs and CPU/memory metrics. Notified SRE channel #sre-support.

2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE Triage (Marco Ruiz): Observed sidecar RSS growth on three nodes; flagged possible memory leak in sidecar prefetch path. Temporarily increased pod restart backoff to force faster recycle for affected nodes.

2026-03-10 10:22 - LensAI (Customer): Provided additional traces showing many short-stream connections followed by periodic longer requests; noted that this pattern started after a client-side traffic shift at 09:35 UTC.

2026-03-10 10:40 - Engineering (R&D - Priya Shah): Correlated telemetry with recent prefetch code change rolled 2026-03-09 (PR #2789). Added hypothesis that new prefetch cache retention with certain short-stream churn causes unbounded map growth.

2026-03-10 11:00 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Scoped mitigation: set sidecar prefetch limit=50 for LensAI pool and cycled sidecar on affected nodes. Observed heartbeats return and autoscaler re-evaluated pool metrics; queued requests drained by 11:07 UTC.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Customer confirmed service returned to normal and requested root-cause writeup and long-term fix timeline.

2026-03-12 14:15 - Priya Shah (Engineering): Created PR to add retention caps and defensive GC to prefetch cache (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2789). Marked as high-priority for hotfix release.
investigation_notes: 1) Memory profiling on sidecar showed steady increase in resident set tied to prefetch cache entries. Leak triggered when short-lived streams created many small prefix caches that were not garbage collected quickly.

2) Heartbeat aggregator drops nodes once heartbeat gap exceeds configured threshold (30s). Autoscaler logic currently treats gap as 'no data' and refuses to expand pool to avoid double-counting, which delayed new slot allocations during this event.

3) The combination of memory leak (sidecar) + conservative autoscaler behavior produced a noisy-neighbor-like symptom: other tenants observed reduced effective share because the pool could not reattach nodes fast enough.
4) Reproduction successful in staging by replaying customer traffic pattern; adding prefetch limits prevented memory growth and kept heartbeats stable.
5) Metrics dashboard snapshots attached in confluence page show RSS growth, heartbeat gap, queue depth and autoscaler decisions timeline.
resolution: Short-term mitigation applied 2026-03-10 10:58: reduced prefetch cache limit to 50 for LensAI pool and cycled sidecar on affected hosts; heartbeats restored and autoscaler reattached nodes; customer traffic recovered by 11:07 UTC.
Medium-term fix: engineering PR to add explicit LRU eviction and periodic GC to prefetch cache (PR #2789). Rolling hotfix scheduled for 2026-03-13 in canary then global rollout pending verification.

Autoscaler change request: open follow-up to make autoscaler tolerant to short heartbeat gaps caused by sidecar restarts — allow speculative scale-up if upstream queue depth rises while heartbeats are missing. Tracking INT task created.
Customer communication: sent post-incident summary and offered proactive monitoring alert for prefetch RSS > 500MB; customer accepted email notification.
follow_up_tasks: INT-XXXX: Update autoscaler logic to consider queue depth when heartbeats are missing (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2026-04-01)

SRE: Add dedicated alert for sustained sidecar RSS growth per node (threshold 600MB for 5m) and bind to on-call routing (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-20)
